Of the ten edge ends, eight join a leaf to a hub, 0.4 in each off-diagonal cell (accent), and two join hub to hub, 0.2; no leaf touches a leaf." width="100%"} The counts of `degree_mixing_dict()` as a matrix: entry `[i][j]` is the fraction (or, with `normalized=False`, the number) of edge ends that join a node of the `i`-th degree to a node of the `j`-th degree. Weight on the diagonal means assortative mixing (similar degrees link up); weight off the diagonal, disassortative mixing. The degree assortativity coefficient is the correlation of this distribution. NetworkX's `degree_mixing_matrix()` returns only the matrix, with an arbitrary order of degrees unless a `mapping=` is given. EdgeCase returns the matrix together with the degrees labelling its rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source_mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's source: `"out"` (default) or `"in"`. [target_mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["in"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : On directed graphs, the degree of each edge's target: `"in"` (default) or `"out"`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether degrees are weighted. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), entries sum to `1`. If `False`, they are counts. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, degrees)`: the square matrix as a list of rows, and the degree values labelling rows and columns, sorted. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star is perfectly disassortative: every edge joins the hub to a leaf, so all the weight sits off the diagonal: ::: {#ec637d1d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec matrix, degrees = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(4).degree_mixing_matrix() degrees, matrix ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([1, 3], [[0.0, 0.5], [0.5, 0.0]]) ``` ::: :::
